rows.original_queue_acceptance: Canonical service/version metadata and release-facing UI/docs identify the resulting release as Relay 1.8.0. ChatGPT can render compact contextual cards for at least Runner project/assignment/preflight state, Source pull request/check/merge state, Cloud release/deployment state, Inspector evidence/review/human-QA state, and durable multi-step operations; cards preserve exact artifact/operation identity, refresh in place where the client supports it, and expand into the shared Relay app/fullscreen view instead of creating parallel mini-products. Cards clearly distinguish queued, working, waiting-on-external-system, waiting-for-human, blocked, stale/unresponsive, failed, rolled-back and complete states. Long-running active operations persist a meaningful heartbeat/updated_at plus human-readable current stage and next action at least every 10 minutes while work is genuinely progressing. By default, 20 minutes without a meaningful heartbeat/progress signal marks an active operation stale; the threshold may be configurable by operation class but must never silently extend itself. Crossing into blocked, failed, stale, waiting-for-human or complete emits one durable notification/attention event; repeated checks do not spam unless the state materially changes. If GitHub/Cloudflare/another dependency is still demonstrably running, Relay says so instead of falsely labeling the worker frozen; if the worker actually stopped heartbeating or hit quota/rate/auth/tool failure, Relay says that plainly and includes the last successful stage plus recovery action. Operation receipts persist stage/state, exact source/head/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, timestamps, retry/reconciliation history and waiting/blocker reasons so reconnecting clients can resume without chat history. Human-QA cards consume the existing Runner QA-helper/Visuals contracts and remain bound to exact evidence identity. Existing headless tools remain compatible; contextual UI is additive. Runner and Inspector retain the 1.7 identities/icons. Web and MCP surfaces use the same state model. Mobile/desktop layouts remain usable. Required tests, exact-head admission, MCP/web rendering checks and authenticated production readback pass before completion.

rows.claim_acceptance: Release as Relay 1.8.0. Required order: (1) durable operation/receipt/liveness model + contextual MCP cards, (2) dashboard/web panel reusing those contracts, (3) broad motion/polish. Card work must encode project context/filter hooks, ordering, overview-state, button and motion primitives so dashboard findings flow back into shared cards instead of diverging. Cards cover Runner project/assignment/preflight, Source PR/check/merge, Cloud release/deploy, Inspector evidence/review/human-QA and multi-step operations; preserve exact identities, refresh where supported, and expand into the shared Relay app. Liveness: meaningful heartbeat/current stage/next action every 5 minutes while progressing; at 10 minutes without meaningful progress surface one possibly-stale warning/check and determine whether an external dependency is still running; at 20 minutes without meaningful progress mark officially stale/unresponsive unless current evidence proves the underlying external job is still active. Blocked, failed, official-stale, waiting-for-human and complete transitions emit one durable attention event; unchanged healthy progress does not spam. Show external waits honestly; quota/rate/auth/tool/dead-heartbeat failures must show last good stage + recovery. Redesign project picker/sidebar to be compact/useful, use available height, avoid an artificially short list, and add practical filtering/search/grouping while keeping project identity legible. Now / Up Next / Finished need stronger hierarchy and newest/recently changed first. Runner, Inspector and `night shift` use identical project-by-project navigation/context mechanics, with distinct compact top overviews: Runner=coordination/execution, Inspector=review/evidence/QA, night shift=unattended activity. Fold Orient → Act → Resolve into that compact page overview where useful instead of a detached strip. Human-facing copy is exactly lowercase `night shift`; never ship `Night Shift`. Buttons must remain obvious buttons: avoid flat highlight fills that read as cards; use depth/press states, stronger text, soft pastel color-matched surfaces, and white text on sufficiently colorful/dark surfaces. Preserve Terra Prime restraint. After structure stabilizes, add ambient system motion, bouncy Field-like glyph motion, tactile transitions/state-change animation and reduced-motion fallbacks. Existing headless clients remain compatible; web/MCP share one state model. New Today/night shift icons + Relay illustrations are NOT a 1.8 blocker. Before completion create an immediate post-release icon-hotfix handoff/assignment; approved assets may land mid-build only if they do not become a dependency. Required tests, exact-head admission, MCP/web rendering checks and authenticated production readback must pass.

Introduce a canonical observed-progress model/receipt/event stream that reconciles Runner coordination state with concrete GitHub and Cloudflare evidence instead of treating claim state, next_action prose, lease presence, or declaration time as execution progress. Each tracked operation/assignment exposes a canonical stage, latest concrete progress event, last meaningful progress timestamp, worker heartbeat/freshness separately from external-system activity, exact known source/base/head/branch/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, waiting/blocker reason, and recovery action. Add reconciliation logic for obvious coordination drift: completed/absorbed/superseded intent must be classifiable separately from live work, orphan/unregistered branches must be surfaced as reconciliation findings, and umbrella/held reservations must not be presented as active execution merely because they still occupy policy capacity. This release does not redesign dashboard/cards and must not write 1.8 UI files. rows.original_queue_goal: Ship Relay 1.9 as the skills-runtime and creative-intelligence release: add a first-class relay.SKILLS system that discovers, validates, versions, resolves and loads portable expertise on demand, then use it to make Relay substantially stronger at aesthetic direction, interaction/flow, motion, platform-native UI craft and performance across web, macOS, Windows, Android and Linux/GNOME while expanding its engineering, GitHub and Cloudflare expertise without bloating the permanent MCP/tool surface.
rows.original_queue_acceptance:
Relay 1.9 ships as a patch train with these canonical capabilities:

- relay.SKILLS: deterministic JIT resolution, bounded context, provenance/license/integrity metadata, capability gating, project-private overlays, safe upstream audit/update, and composable creative/platform/performance/GitHub/Cloudflare skills. Creative coverage includes aesthetic direction, IA/flow, motion, visual QA, optimization, web, macOS, Windows, Android and GNOME; Figma-bound skills use the real dependency when available.
- worker communication: inspect sibling live state first; classify FYI/request/blocker/decision/handoff/scope-change; cite exact project/assignment/branch/PR/evidence identity; communicate context, impact and requested action; reconcile received messages against canonical state before acting; avoid duplicate/no-op chatter. Messages never silently change ownership/scope: Runner amend/rescope/handoff remains authoritative.
- organization-first narration: later coordination successors must consume canonical staff identity and describe people + ownership + outcome + validation by default; preserve machine IDs/evidence underneath and keep low-level transport/tool/SHA detail subordinate unless directly relevant. Relationship adaptation stays Julian/lead-managed; no canned joke bank.
- assignment taxonomy: durable amendable category, labels, tags and designated role metadata. Controlled categories include architecture, design, implementation, research, QA/verification, maintenance, release and coordination. Labels are structured cross-cutting metadata; tags are bounded freeform discovery/context metadata. One primary role plus optional supporting roles may drive skill selection/communication posture but never authorization. Role metadata is separate from sticky staff identity; names come from the canonical staff directory. Expose taxonomy/roles to routing, filtering, UI and resume checkpoints.
- live amendment sync: active workers/chats consume only new relevant canonical amendments from a monotonic cursor at bounded synchronization points; unchanged checks inject nothing, and scope-changing/blocking updates reconcile before conflicting work continues.
- safe assignment amendments: stable identity/ownership, immutable claimed branch/base, CAS/readback, conflict-safe scope changes, bounded who/when/what/why history. Planning skills amend canonical state rather than hand-edit it.
- findings-ledger routing: classify adopt/defer/reject/supersede; route adopted findings into the safest existing assignment or deliberate successor; maintain RFS linkage/status. Ledger is planning input, not automatic backlog.
- low-overhead resume checkpoints from canonical evidence: assignment/branch/base/head, changed paths, commits, PR/check/deploy stage, last successful action, blockers/waits, next action, QA context, ledger refs and exact evidence identities; dedupe unchanged state and expose latest-valid resume.
- universal meaningful x.x.# cadence: test/admit exact source; merge; deploy if applicable; verify runtime/readback; refresh integrations/consumer when needed; verify the new surface; continue from canonical state.
- valid work must not be blocked by file/document/context/request-size ceilings: switch automatically to patch/edit, append, bounded chunks, indexed/sharded logical docs and deterministic reassembly while preserving ownership/provenance/CAS safety.
- preserve Relay 1.8 UI contracts: human headline + short description, subordinate technical detail, specific QA asks, live previews when viable with exact identity.

Tests cover taxonomy/roles, communication/handoffs, amendments, ledger routing, resume, size-safe transport, skill gating and UI/QA. No parallel state store, giant permanent prompt dump, one-tool-per-skill explosion or new standing credentials.
